title: Glossary
summary: Definitions of the terms used throughout the Subject Headings Manual: kinds of headings (form, topical, name, straight, inverted), kinds of subdivisions and their MARC subfields ($x topical, $v form, $y chronological, $z geographic), qualifiers (adjectival, geographic, parenthetical), free-floating subdivisions, references (BT, NT, RT, UF, general see / see also), and authority file concepts.
validation_rules: A subject heading string consists of an $a element optionally followed by subdivisions in $v, $x, $y, and/or $z; a "string" is a heading with at least one subdivision. (Glossary: Subject heading; String)

Topical subdivisions are $x, form subdivisions are $v, chronological (period) subdivisions are $y, geographic (place) subdivisions are $z. (Glossary: Topical subdivision; Form subdivision; Chronological subdivision; Geographic subdivision)

In indirect geographic subdivision the larger geographic entity is placed in a separate $z before the more specific locality; in direct subdivision the place name is used without an interposed larger entity. (Glossary: Geographic subdivision)

An inverted heading places the noun first, followed by a comma and the adjective (e.g. `Diplomatic and consular service, Egyptian`); a straight heading uses natural word order (e.g. `English poetry`). (Glossary: Inverted heading; Adjectival qualifier; Straight heading)

A geographic qualifier is the name of a larger entity in parentheses after a more specific place or entity (e.g. `Whitney, Mount (Calif.)`, `Gobi Desert (Mongolia and China)`, `Colorado River (Colo.-Mexico)`, `Empire State Building (New York, N.Y.)`). (Glossary: Geographic qualifier)

A parenthetical qualifier disambiguates or clarifies a heading (e.g. `Plates (Engineering)`, `Plates (Tableware)`, `BASIC (Computer program language)`, `Adonis (Greek deity)`). (Glossary: Parenthetical qualifier)
Free-floating subdivisions may be assigned under designated headings without an authority record for the specific string. (Glossary: Free-floating subdivision)
Corporate-name subheadings are in $b of X10 fields and, in display, separated from the main heading by a period (e.g. `United States. Congress. House`). (Glossary: Subheading)
4XX fields are use (UF) references from non-valid terms; such a term is not valid as a subject heading. (Glossary: Use reference)
